founder.title: Founder & CEO
founder.bio: Cristina Mancini is the visionary Founder & CEO of Beyond Code Collective (BCC), a new national ecosystem built to close the AI literacy gap and unlock digital dignity for communities long excluded from the future of work. She created BCC to answer a transformative question: What if every community had permanent, culturally grounded access to the skills and pathways that define the next decade of innovation and the future of work?
founder.quote: "AI doesn't eliminate the need for technical literacy; it makes it more essential. At BCC we're teaching our talent how to supervise it, secure it, and build with it. You cannot supervise what you do not understand. This is why foundational knowledge is critical."

items.title: The AI Job Nobody Explains, and Why We're Teaching It
items.excerpt: Fonz Morris on the Forward Deployed Engineer — the fastest-growing role in AI, the one almost nobody has an on-ramp into, and the program Beyond Code Collective is building around it.
items.imageAlt: A Beyond Code Collective cohort together in the studio
items.body:
I've made twenty-four videos about one job title. Thirty to forty seconds each, one a day. Most people still haven't heard of it.

MIT put out a number that started this for me: ninety-five percent of AI pilots fail. That number isn't about the models. Every company can buy the same models now. They fail because nobody in the building knows how to make one work inside a real business.

That gap has a job title. Forward Deployed Engineer. You sit down next to the person actually doing the work, find the real bottleneck behind whatever they told you the problem was, and build something that runs on Monday.

Palantir invented the role. OpenAI posted one at two hundred eighty thousand base, no CS degree required. Anthropic, Microsoft and Databricks are all hiring for it.

Then look at who's getting in. Most listings want three to seven years of experience. Anthropic said they would train tens of thousands of AI engineers. I went looking for how many actually got trained and found eighty-six.

I know that gap from the inside. Self-taught designer out of Bed-Stuy. I got to Netflix because I stayed at an event in San Francisco I almost left early, and somebody I met there knew my old manager. That is not a plan you can hand to anybody. Once I was in, we started Pathways, because getting in the room yourself isn't the same as building a door.

Here is why I think this one can be taught. The hardest skill in the job isn't writing code. It's judgment: which step of a workflow should be ordinary software, which one actually needs a model, and which one stays with a person. Right behind judgment is evals, proving the thing works against real cases that already happened, and that part takes almost no code at all.

Both of those favor somebody who has worked a real job in a real industry. Eight years in claims processing teaches you things about claims processing I will never know, and in this job that counts for more than a certificate. That describes a lot of the people we serve at Beyond Code Collective.

The jobs are there. The on-ramp isn't. That's what we're building.

— Fonz Morris
items.author: Fonz Morris

items.title: Kleon Penn Passes CompTIA Tech+ on His First Try
items.excerpt: Kleon Penn is part of the very first Beyond the Game cohort — the group that had to be the proof the model worked. He just passed the CompTIA Tech+ exam on his first attempt, with a score of 700.
items.imageAlt: Kleon Penn, Beyond the Game first cohort, passed CompTIA Tech+ on his first attempt
items.body:
Kleon Penn is part of our initial Beyond the Game cohort, the first group of students to go through the program. That matters. The first cohort had no older students to look to, no proof yet that the model worked. They were the proof. When Kleon joined, IT certifications were a goal on a whiteboard. Now they're on his resume: he passed the CompTIA Tech+ exam on his first attempt, with a score of 700.

If you've never sat for a cert exam, here's the context. Tech+ covers hardware, software, networking basics, security, and troubleshooting. It's the exam that tells employers you understand how technology works, not just how to use it. A lot of people take it two or three times. Kleon walked in once and walked out certified.

He earned that score the boring way, with study sessions and practice exams, going back over whatever he missed until it stuck. Credit also goes to his instructor, Kobie Joyner, who taught the cohort through the full Tech+ curriculum and pushed the class to treat practice exams like the real thing. Kobie has now guided two cohorts through this material, including the one our program lead Ramon Clemente came through, and results like Kleon's are what that teaching looks like on paper.

Tech+ is the first credential on a track that leads to Network+, Security+, and real jobs in IT. Ramon took the same first step on his own path. Kleon is right behind him, with a plan to keep stacking certifications.

Congratulations, Kleon. First try. We see you.

If his story sounds like something you want for yourself, the program is open.

items.title: Ramon Clemente Passed Two IT Certifications. He's Not Done.
items.excerpt: Ramon Clemente spent years playing basketball before he took over Beyond the Game. This year he became the program's best argument — passing CompTIA Tech+ and Network+, with a security certification up next.
items.imageAlt: Ramon Clemente, Head of Beyond the Game, passed CompTIA Tech+ and Network+
items.body:
Ramon Clemente spent years playing basketball before he took over Beyond the Game, our program for athletes working out what comes after sports. This year he became the program's best argument.

Ramon passed the CompTIA Tech+ and Network+ exams, studying under Kobie Joyner, the instructor for his cohort's certification track. Neither exam is a formality. Tech+ covers hardware, software, and troubleshooting fundamentals. Network+ covers how systems connect, and a lot of people fail it at least once. Ramon passed both, and his next target is Security+.

He's not just collecting certs. Less than a year into the transition, Ramon is building apps, leaning on AI tools to prototype things that used to require a whole team.

The reason we're writing about this: Ramon asks his students to believe a former athlete can start over in tech. It's a much easier ask when the guy running the program just did it.

"I ask my guys to believe they can start over. I couldn't ask that if I hadn't done it myself — same classes, same exams, same late nights. The game taught me how to prepare; Kobie showed me what to prepare for." — Ramon Clemente, Head of Beyond the Game

If you're an athlete wondering what your next chapter looks like, come talk to him.

items.title: What's Coming Up: Free Summer Workshops at The Forge ATL
items.excerpt: From design and game-making to vibe coding and digital storytelling — here's everything Beyond Code Collective has on the calendar this summer. Every session is free and hosted at ATDC in Atlanta.
items.imageAlt: Learners and instructors during a Beyond Code Collective workshop
items.body:
Summer at The Forge: ATL is packed. Over the coming weeks, Beyond Code Collective is hosting a series of free, hands-on workshops at the Advanced Technology Development Center (ATDC) in Atlanta — covering design, game development, AI, entrepreneurship, and more. Here's what's on the calendar.

DESIGN YOUR WORLD — Making Your Ideas Look as Good as They Feel · Monday, June 29 at 11:00 AM · ATDC. Learn the design fundamentals that make your ideas land as well as they feel.

GAME ON — Stop Playing Games. Start Making Them. · Saturday, July 11 at 11:00 AM · ATDC. Go from player to creator and build your first game.

Replit for Wisdom Leaders Bootcamp (55+) · Monday, July 20 at 11:00 AM · ATDC. A welcoming, hands-on intro to building with Replit, designed for learners 55 and up.

Vibe Coding Workshop w/ Replit · Thursday, July 23 at 11:00 AM · ATDC. Bring an idea and build it live using AI-assisted coding tools.

Putting Yourself Out There: Digital Storytelling for Entrepreneurs · Friday, July 24 at 1:00 PM · ATDC. Craft the story behind your venture and learn to share it with confidence.

Breakfast Chat — AI in Education with Educators & Parents · Tuesday, July 28 at 11:00 AM · ATDC. An open conversation about how AI is reshaping learning, for the adults guiding the next generation.

All sessions are free, but space is limited. Reserve your seat for any of these events on Eventbrite.

On March 9, The Forge hosted its opening event at North Star AI Labs inside Georgia Tech's Advanced Technology Development Center, convening some of Atlanta's leading educators, technologists, and community leaders.

items.body:
Beyond The Game — our national, cohort-based workforce program for transitioning professional and NCAA student-athletes — has opened its waitlist for the Summer 2026 cohort.

The part-time, 6–9 month program pairs industry-recognized CompTIA certifications with wraparound support, from professional communication to mental health resources, helping athletes design and enter a durable second career.

Upon completion, participants are placed in paid externships and apprenticeships with partner employers. Sign up now to reserve your spot and get updates on enrollment.

items.title: Beyond Code Collective Launches to Expand AI Literacy and Prepare the Next Generation of Tech Leaders
items.excerpt: The standalone nonprofit will serve as an integrated ecosystem with virtual and place-based skills-building programs, equipping learners of all backgrounds with the skills to thrive in a tech-driven economy.
items.imageAlt: Cristina Mancini, Founder & CEO of Beyond Code Collective
items.body:
Black Girls Code announced today the formation of Beyond Code Collective™, an independent nonprofit organization that bridges the gap between inspiration, training, and employment in tech, connecting learners to educational content, opportunities to develop cutting-edge technologies, and avenues to launch careers.

Beyond Code Collective is focused on demystifying the digital landscape and creating sustainable career pathways for individuals at every stage of life to participate and thrive in a rapidly evolving tech-driven workforce. The nonprofit starts from a simple belief: tech is the tool, people are the power.

Beyond Code has developed a comprehensive curriculum program with input from leading tech companies, academics, and experts, including Zapier, the leading AI orchestration platform. Beyond Code is also collaborating with the Responsible AI for Computational Action design-based research project — a curriculum out of MIT's RAISE Initiative — to offer AI, machine learning, and emerging technologies curricula for middle and high school-aged participants.

"At Beyond Code Collective, we're uniting the worlds of emerging tech and human talent to shape a future where innovation is inclusive, responsible, and within reach for all," said Cristina Mancini, Founder and CEO. "I founded this new organization to address the growing gap between skills and opportunities across all communities."

Beyond Code Collective will offer the following programs: The Forge — intergenerational, place-based hubs blending tech education, community engagement, and workforce development; Beyond Code Catalysts — a cohort-based workforce program creating pathways into high-demand tech careers; and Beyond The Game — a national program for transitioning professional and NCAA student-athletes.

items.title: Future Cod3rs Camp: BCC Partners with Holberton to Bring Coding & Leadership to Youth in Puerto Rico
items.excerpt: This June, BCC and Holberton Coding School are offering a two-week, full-day coding and leadership program for youth ages 10–14 in San Juan, PR. Scholarships available.
items.imageAlt: Students and instructors at Beyond Code Collective's Puerto Rico summer camp
items.body:
This June, Beyond Code Collective is partnering with Holberton Coding School to offer the Future Cod3rs Camp — a two-week, full-day coding and leadership program for youth ages 10–14 in San Juan, Puerto Rico.

The camp runs June 15–26, 2026, from 8:30 AM to 3:30 PM at Holberton Coding School (1550 PR-25, San Juan, PR 00909). Instruction is in Spanish, lunch and snacks are provided, and scholarships are available.

"If we don't teach the next generation to build the tools of tomorrow, they'll be left behind."
— Cristina Mancini, CEO, Beyond Code Collective

This builds on BCC's growing impact in Puerto Rico. Our inaugural 2025 summer camp, hosted at Atlantic University in partnership with Vimenti School, saw students in grades 6–7 complete projects in animation, game design, photography, cinematography, esports, and cybersecurity.

Alongside that camp, BCC hosted Build a Beat — a community event drawing 100 attendees and professionals from Puerto Rico's tech, music, and education sectors. The event was covered by El Nuevo Día, Metro PR, and other major local outlets, and deepened BCC's partnerships with Atlantic University, El Beatdown, DDEC, government leadership, and local employers.

In March 2026, BCC also led a workshop for seventh-grade students at Vimenti School in celebration of Women's History Month. Students learned about women in STEM and coded a virtual gratitude card for inspiring women in their lives using block coding on the Scratch platform.

To register for the Future Cod3rs Camp or inquire about scholarships, contact Jeannette Firpo at jeannette.firpo@wearebcc.org.

items.title: Beyond Code Collective Announces The Forge, An Intergenerational Innovation and Workforce Hub
items.excerpt: The first Forge residency launches in Atlanta in partnership with Georgia Tech's Advanced Technology Development Center, offering free programming for learners of all ages starting March 21.
items.imageAlt: Panelists on stage at The Forge opening event at Georgia Tech ATDC
items.body:
Beyond Code Collective today announced the launch of The Forge with the opening of its first residency site in Atlanta, Georgia.

The Forge is a new network of intergenerational, site-specific hubs that blend technology education, community engagement, and workforce development under one roof. The Forge: ATL, hosted within North Star AI Labs at Georgia Tech's Advanced Technology Development Center (ATDC), will offer free programming two days a week, beginning March 21 through August 2026.

"We are thrilled to formally launch The Forge, designed to be a true 'third place' that is neither school nor work, where middle schoolers sit alongside mid-career professionals, and families with their kids, as they explore AI and emerging technology in a safe space to ask questions without fear or shame," said Cristina Mancini, Founder and CEO of Beyond Code Collective.

To celebrate the residency, The Forge hosted an opening event on March 9, convening some of Atlanta's leading educators, technologists, and community leaders. Panelists included Georgia Representative Kim Schofield, Technology and Social Impact Strategist Darrell Booker, and Professional Basketball Player Ramón Clemente.

Designed in collaboration with local stakeholders, each Forge center delivers culturally responsive programming to its community, serving K-12 students and adults seeking pathways into tech-driven careers.

items.title: Beyond Code Collective Announces Leadership Team and Tech Futures National Council
items.excerpt: Beyond Code appoints Mica Le John as Executive Director, Jihan Johnston-McGlotten as Managing Director of The Forge, and Ramon Clemente as Head of Beyond The Game — alongside a distinguished Tech Futures National Council.
items.imageAlt: Mica Le John, Executive Director of Beyond Code Collective
items.body:
Beyond Code Collective today announced the formation of its Tech Futures National Council and appointed three key leaders to advance its mission of preparing individuals across generations to seize the opportunities of a tech-powered world.

Mica Le John joins as Executive Director, serving as the CEO's execution partner supporting the organization's expansion, program development, brand visibility, and community impact. Le John brings over a decade of experience at the intersection of technology, creativity, and social impact, transitioning from leading strategic partnerships and innovation at Black Girls Code.

Jihan Johnston-McGlotten joins as Managing Director of The Forge, Beyond Code's network of intergenerational, site-specific hubs that integrate technology education, community engagement, and workforce development. Johnston-McGlotten brings over a decade of experience building tech communities and is leading growth and expansion of The Forge in Atlanta.

Ramon Clemente joins after a 17-year professional basketball career as Head of Beyond The Game, a national, cohort-based workforce program for transitioning professional and NCAA student-athletes.

"I founded Beyond Code Collective because innovation must include everyone and technology should be a bridge to opportunity, not a barrier," said Cristina Mancini, Founder and CEO. "Together, we're not just focused on closing the digital divide but ensuring communities aren't left behind."

The Tech Futures National Council brings together leaders from NASA, YouTube, Xbox, the University of Texas at Austin, and more — providing strategic insight and real-world perspectives to inform curricula and programming across AI literacy, innovation pathways, and workforce development.
